findings.detail: 11 of the 12 scholarship pages had a meta description built from a template that included the funder name, running 167 to 210 characters (Government of Ireland International Education Scholarships was worst, at 210). Shortened the template to drop the funder and the restated keyword list. This field is meta-only, nothing on the page or the /tools/scholarships listing reuses this exact string as visible copy, so it was safe to edit.

suggestions.title: No structured data at all on the /tools funnel, /software and /blog index
suggestions.detail: Checked all 52 sitemap URLs: the homepage and every /study/* destination page carry a valid @graph of JSON-LD (Organization, WebSite, SoftwareApplication, FAQPage), and every individual scholarship page has its own FAQPage block. But /software, /blog and /tools themselves, plus all nine /tools/* calculators (eligibility, cost, loan, checklist, document-checklist, universities, scholarships, compare, cv-maker), have no application/ld+json block whatsoever, confirmed by a raw fetch of each, not just a parsing miss. These are exactly the free tools the brief calls the top of the funnel.
suggestions.why: Adding the right schema (SoftwareApplication or WebApplication for the calculators, CollectionPage or ItemList for the three index pages) is an editorial call about which @type fits an interactive tool rather than an article, and getting the type wrong is worse than leaving it out, so this wants a person's decision rather than a mechanical add.

summary:
Site: up, 200, sitemap valid with 52 URLs, all 200.
Audit: crawled all 52 pages; the only real finding was 11 scholarship pages with a meta description 167-210 characters long, fixed (meta-only, not visible copy). Everything else checked clean: robots.txt, tenant-subdomain noindex, canonicals, alt text, heading order, internal links.
Published: nothing today. Both keyword queues have zero todo rows right now; the one blocked B2B row (Nepal's 2083 consultancy regulation) got real research progress but not a primary source I could cite, so it stays blocked rather than being guessed at.
Blocked: the Search Console indexing check and GA figures, because this run's own credential-materialization safeguard would not turn the present service-account key into an API call; that needs a person's call, not a missing credential.
Worth a look: twelve pages, the /tools funnel, /software and /blog indexes, have no structured data at all, unlike every other page on the site.
